correctness.rationale: PASS: The 27 ternary words under at-most-one nonwrap +1 coordinate error have exact balls of size 1..4. Nine explicitly displayed three-word conflict blocks partition all 27 and are pairwise incompatible within each block, giving |C|<=9. The parity-corner eight plus 111 achieves nine with disjoint balls. Independent search rebuilt the balls, verified every pair in all nine blocks, and found exactly one labeled compatible nine-code; this is finite EXHAUSTIVE over all 27 words. It matches Cassuto et al residue-mod-2 lift of binary {000,111}.

evidence: Cassuto Theorem 4 and Theorem 7: general sufficient modular lifting; Theorem 8: sphere-packing bound for WRAPAROUND model.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Those broader correction claims yield feasible codes but neither the sharp nonwrap upper bound nor uniqueness of all optimal length-three ternary codes. Wraparound is a different channel and its sphere bound cannot simply be substituted.

originality.rationale: PASS best-of-knowledge: Cassuto-Schwartz-Bohossian-Bruck 2007 explicitly gives the modulo-2 lifted construction and its correction property, so the nine-word code is preexisting and NOT novel. Its inspected entire five-page preprint discusses construction, general decoding, perfect wraparound cases and length7 Hamming instance, but states no nonwrap ternary length3 sharp bound or unique labeled maximum. Exact finite classification is not implied by construction alone; residual risk of an unindexed enumeration.
residual_risks: An obscure finite code table may already contain length-three nonwrap upper bound and uniqueness.
Scope restricted to all 27 labeled words at q=3, length3, at most one +1 error; no generalization.
